findings.title: Authority safety fixture rejects a benign freshness bound
findings.detail: The authority test bans any dataclass field containing limit, so it rejects DriftPolicy.freshness_limit even though that field is only the explicit maximum evidence age used to reject stale research evidence. The executable import and call safety checks pass, and this lexical failure supplies no evidence of deployment, execution or risk-limit authority.

findings.title: Tamper fixture mutates the shared champion across tests
findings.detail: The tamper test changes rerolled.inputs.champion.role with object.__setattr__, but that champion aliases the module-level CHAMPION fixture and is not restored. A later regression fixture therefore receives ROLE_MISMATCH and becomes order-dependent; the LEARN implementation itself correctly rejects the contaminated input fail-closed.

findings.title: Proof-mismatch fixture also creates a self-comparison
findings.detail: Run 38 assigns CHALLENGER_PROPOSAL to the champion while the default challenger already uses that same proposal. The input therefore violates the earlier self-comparison invariant before proof binding, so SELF_COMPARISON is the correct deterministic first reason rather than the asserted PROOF_MODEL_MISMATCH. Give the mislabelled champion a distinct proposal identity whose supplied proof is bound to a different proposal, preserving both fail-closed checks and testing only the intended invariant.

findings.title: Transition-order fixture also supplies future evidence
findings.detail: Run 38 backdates effective_at to CREATED minus one day but retains the helper's default evidence, which is available only at EFFECTIVE. The evidence is therefore unknowable at the backdated instant, so EVIDENCE_NOT_KNOWABLE_AT_AS_OF is the correct deterministic first reason before the ModelTransition chronology guard can return TRANSITION_NOT_ORDERED. Supply evidence available no later than the backdated instant so the fixture isolates transition ordering; do not weaken either fail-closed check.
